words.gloss: of those who do not hate (loving ones)

literal: Even if they speak like those who are not attached, the words of those who do not hate will be quickly understood.
translation: Even if they speak like strangers who care nothing for us, the words of those who harbor no anger are quickly understood in their true sense.
modern: நம்மிடம் அன்பு இல்லாத அந்நியரைப் போலப் பேசினாலும், நம்மிடம் வெறுப்பு இல்லாத காதலரின் சொற்களின் உண்மையான குறிப்பு விரைவாகப் புரிந்து கொள்ளப்படும்.
explanation: This couplet from the chapter 'Reading the Signs' describes the deep, unspoken understanding between lovers. Sometimes, a lover might speak cold or distant words, acting like an unattached stranger (uṟāatavar). However, because they do not actually harbor any anger or hatred (ceṟāar), their true loving intent behind those words is quickly (ollai) perceived (uṇarappaṭum) by the partner. The couplet highlights how true affection cannot be masked by superficial coldness, as the heart's real intention is easily read.
